title: US PCE nowcast – Past the oil-shock peak
gist: Oxford Economics' nowcast sees headline US PCE inflation decelerating to 3.7% y/y in June from a May peak above 4%, as falling energy prices offset core goods inflation that stays elevated on an AI-demand-driven memory chip shortage.

insights.claim: Headline PCE inflation is projected to decelerate to 3.7% year-on-year in June, following a peak of over 4% in May.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A confirmed peak-and-roll-over in headline PCE would support the case that price pressures are cresting, a key input for Fed policy expectations and rate-sensitive positioning.
insights.quote: Headline PCE inflation is projected to decelerate to 3.7% year-on-year in June, following a peak of over 4% in May.
insights.locator: Headline PCE inflation is projected to decelerate

insights.claim: The projected June deceleration in headline PCE is primarily driven by lower energy prices, which carry a smaller weight in the PCE index than in the CPI.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Because PCE and CPI weight energy differently, the same oil-driven decline in gasoline prices will show up as a smaller relief in CPI than in PCE, so investors comparing the two gauges should expect PCE to look softer than CPI over this period.
insights.quote: This decline is primarily driven by lower energy prices, which have a smaller weight in the PCE index compared to the CPI.
insights.locator: This decline is primarily driven by lower energy prices

insights.claim: Motor fuel costs dropped nearly 10%, a key driver of the relief in headline inflation past the oil-shock peak.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A near-10% drop in motor fuel costs is a concrete, trackable input to the disinflation story; a reversal in fuel prices would quickly reintroduce upside risk to headline PCE.
insights.quote: a nearly 10% drop in motor fuel costs
insights.locator: While energy prices, including a nearly 10% drop

themes.theme: AI-driven chip shortage keeps core goods inflation sticky

insights.claim: Core goods inflation remains elevated because of a memory chip shortage that is linked to AI demand, even as energy prices fall.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: AI-driven demand for memory chips is acting as an independent inflation channel in tech hardware; investors should watch memory/semiconductor supply-demand balance as a driver of both core goods CPI/PCE and chipmaker pricing power.
insights.quote: core goods inflation remains elevated due to a memory chip shortage linked to AI demand
insights.locator: While energy prices, including a nearly 10% drop

insights.claim: In June, core PCE prices are expected to rise 0.2%, driven in part by increases in computer software and accessories prices.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: Software and accessories pricing is a specific line item feeding the AI-related inflation narrative, useful for investors tracking whether tech-sector price increases are broadening beyond hardware.
insights.quote: In June, core PCE prices are expected to rise by 0.2%, influenced by increases in computer software and accessories.
insights.locator: In June, core PCE prices are expected to rise

insights.claim: The Federal Reserve is likely to hold its current policy stance until late 2027 while it waits for sustainable progress toward its 2% inflation target.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: A hold into late 2027 implies a longer higher-for-longer rate regime than markets may be pricing if they extrapolate from the June PCE deceleration alone, relevant for rate and duration positioning.
insights.quote: The Federal Reserve is likely to maintain its current stance until late 2027, anticipating sustainable progress towards its 2% inflation target.
insights.locator: The Federal Reserve is likely to maintain

insights.claim: Methodological changes coming in September may lead to downward revisions in core goods inflation, particularly in the technology sector.
insights.speaker: Emma Pollard
insights.so_what: The current tech-driven core goods inflation reading could be overstated and revised lower in September, so investors should treat the AI/chip-shortage inflation narrative as provisional pending the methodology update.
insights.quote: The upcoming methodological changes in September may lead to downward revisions in core goods inflation, particularly in the technology sector.
insights.locator: The upcoming methodological changes in September
